title: Defect cards
description: The defects a campaign is reconciling, exported from whatever tracker the project uses, as a flat array. Its purpose is to let a reader join a journey to the tracker items that describe it WITHOUT reaching into the tracker, and to let a reconciliation distinguish a defect the campaign found from one that already existed — which is the difference between a campaign that discovered something and one that inventoried what was already known. Nothing here is a coverage figure: a card's `state` is a tracker's opinion, not evidence, and a card marked done is not a journey proved. The vocabulary of `state` belongs to the project's tracker and is never enumerated here.

id.description: The tracker's own identifier, exactly as the tracker renders it. Every other artefact joins on this string, so it must not be normalised, prefixed or re-cased on export.

n.description: The numeric part of the id, when the tracker has one. Carried separately only so a reader can sort chronologically without parsing the id; never use it as an identity.

state.description: The tracker's workflow state, verbatim. An OPEN vocabulary owned by the project's tracker — 'Done', 'Todo', 'Needs More Work' and 'Backlog' are one project's words. A reader must not map an unrecognised state onto done or not-done; it shows the state as written and counts it separately.

title.description: The defect in one line, stated as the observed wrong behaviour rather than as the proposed fix. A title naming a fix hides what was measured.

desc.description: The card body, usually Markdown, carrying the measurement: what was probed, what came back, and which hypotheses were eliminated. This is the field a reconciliation reads to decide whether a defect was measured or merely suspected, so exporting a truncated body degrades the ledger that consumes it.

origin.description: Whether this card was raised BY the campaign or already existed when it started. The distinction is what makes a campaign's yield measurable: without it, a tracker full of pre-existing defects reads as a campaign that found a great deal. `found` means this campaign raised it; `original` means it predated the campaign. A project with a third category should name it rather than force it into these two.

flows.description: Journey ids from the flow specification that this defect breaks, when the join is known. Optional because most trackers do not carry it — and a card with no flows is not a card affecting no journeys, it is a card nobody joined.

surface.description: The surface the defect is on, when it is surface-scoped.

severity.description: How much it costs, in the project's own vocabulary. An OPEN vocabulary.

url.description: Link back to the tracker item, so a reader can leave the campaign surface for the authority.
